definition: Concoct means to make up an untrue account.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word concoct. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know concoct should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Rather than confess he had forgotten the anniversary, he concocted a tale about a marvelous surprise that had 'fallen through at the last minute.'
Overstate is the mildest rung, well below concoct — an overstated report heats up real events, but real events are still in the pan.
Fudge stops short of concoct: to fudge is to blur or nudge true numbers, while to concoct is to cook the entire dish from nothing.

Cook up is the informal twin of concoct — same kitchen, same dishonest recipe, a story thrown together fast when the truth is inconvenient. Concoct is the slightly dressier word a novelist or a narrator reaches for; cook up is what the culprit's friends would say.

To dream up is to invent something new — a gadget, a game, a plot for a film — with no dishonesty implied at all. Concoct points the invention at deception: a concocted account is assembled from nothing precisely so that someone will mistake it for the truth.

In 1902, a man calling himself Professor Aldous Renwick arrived in Cleveland with a leather trunk and a business proposition.
For a fee, he would trace any family's line back to nobility.
The results were remarkably consistent: every client, it turned out, descended from a baron.
Renwick did not research so much as concoct.
He invented castles, forged parish registers, and once supplied three unrelated families with the same crusader ancestor.
The scheme unraveled when two proud clients compared their commissioned family trees at a dinner party and found the identical knight at the top of each.
Renwick left town that week.
The trunk, seized by the sheriff, held blank certificates, a book of heraldry, and a list of forty names he had not yet gotten to.
